newsitem.title: PERU: Power blackout heightens tension in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Power blackout heightens tension in Peru.

text.p: A power blackout affecting large parts of Lima heightened tension in the early hours of Christmas Day on Wednesday as the holiday period remained overshadowed by the guerrilla takeover of the Japanese ambassador's residence.
Although the cuts brought immediate speculation of guerrilla attacks on electricity installations, company officials insisted the problem was due to a surge in demand.
"At Christmas there is a high demand for energy, which pressures the circuits," said Alberto Alegria, of local electricity distributor Edelnor.

The zones affected included the middle-class residential district of San Isidro, where about 20 Marxist rebels from the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) were holding 105 VIP hostages for the eighth day.
Peru's guerrilla movements, in armed conflict with the government for 16 years, have traditionally marked the Christmas and New Year periods with attacks on electricity installations.

However, such attacks have subsided in recent years as the government gained the upper hand in the war on insurgency. The MRTA and the larger Shining Path were thought to have been virtually defeated until the dramatic attack on the Japanese ambassador's home indicated their ability to strike back.
